package: P3 — drawer, OSD, accessibility semantics, and visual proof

source_identity.description: Exact pre-P2/P3 product baseline rendered from a temporary git archive, not a worktree

candidate_identity.description: P3 candidate plus a separate footer-clearance and enabled-semantics repair; the repair commit SHA is reported by package closeout

capture.fixture: Real PlayerView and PlayerCoordinator widgets; six synthetic audio tracks, six synthetic subtitle tracks plus Off; selected rows audio 1 and subtitle 11; no pending request; selected row receives initial focus; paused 32:00/2:00:00 playback; fixed 2026-09-22T20:00:00Z clock; no real artwork or media
capture.matched_inputs: Before and after use the same capture test, fixture, viewport, DPR, text scale, scene, playback state, focus, selection, pending state, and fonts
capture.background_match: Exact pixel comparison of a left-side crop outside the drawer/fade returned zero differing pixels for all eight before/after pairs

inspection.reviewed: All 16 images inspected in four matched before/after contact sheets and at original resolution
inspection.differences: Track copy and its resulting line wrapping changed: raw language/codec labels became the approved primary/supporting hierarchy. The repair reserves scroll-viewport clearance above the fixed footer at 1280x720. Drawer width, fade, gradient, header, close control, dividers, selected fill, checkmark, footer placement and styling, and scene placement remain unchanged.
inspection.legibility: Primary/supporting hierarchy remains legible over both bright and dark scenes at both required sizes. The selected row and focus remain visually distinct.
inspection.long_peers: At 1920x1080, both long identical-prefix peers and their theatrical/commentary tails are visible. At 1280x720, the matched initial frame shows the theatrical subtitle peer and only the leading portion of the next audio peer; it does not show both subtitle peers. The 1280 widget proof scrolls/focuses both peers, verifies both full tails are rendered and inside the viewport, and leaves the commentary peer focused.
inspection.limits: Static portable widget renders do not establish moving-video contrast, native overlay composition, physical DPI, Windows focus/input, or Narrator behavior.

repair.reason: Wrapped rows could consume the footer's bottom region at 1280x720 because the scroll viewport used all space above the footer without dedicated clearance.
repair.change: Reserve 24 geometry-scale points below the track scroll viewport while retaining the approved rail geometry, typography, colors, and footer placement; expose explicit enabled state on labeled OSD action semantics.
repair.recapture: All eight after images were regenerated from the same fixture. Only the four 1280x720 images changed; all four 1920x1080 hashes remained stable.

adaptive_widget_proof.test: track panel scales its reading rail and soft fade through 4K
adaptive_widget_proof.assertions: No layout exception; protected rail/fade geometry and gradient retained; long visible label stays inside the rail and scroll viewport; selected row remains focused; complete tooltip and semantics identity remain available.
adaptive_widget_proof.reachability: A separate 256-row widget test scrolls to row 256 at 800x600 and 1280x720 while retaining Close and without overflow.
adaptive_widget_proof.footer_clearance: The 1280 audio/subtitle test `1280 track drawers keep wrapped rows clear of the fixed footer` verifies the footer is inside the rail, visible row intersections do not overlap it, both identical-prefix peers become fully visible through keyboard focus scrolling with distinguishable tails, the last peer retains focus, and no layout exception occurs.

privacy: All names, labels, scenes, paths, timing, and metadata are synthetic. No Plex credentials, tokens, private media metadata, filenames, server responses, or real playback logs are present.
claims_boundary: Portable Flutter widget composition, geometry, focus, interaction, semantics-tree, and deterministic static-render evidence only. No physical Windows, Narrator, moving-video, native overlay, label-to-output, packaging, or user visual-approval claim.
